key_insight: Multideterminant QMC barely changes excitation energies but is crucial for capturing exciton localization in low-density solid molecular hydrogen.
engineering_relevance: Accurate localization is needed to predict optical transition strengths and excitation-induced forces, which excitation energies alone may not reliably characterize.
method: Model phase-I molecular hydrogen under increasing compression using QMC.
Compare single-orbital substitutions with multideterminant expansions covering all single particle–hole transitions.
Benchmark against BSE and TDDFT across nuclear configurations representing thermal and quantum fluctuations.
evidence_signal: Multideterminant QMC generally agrees with BSE on localization, transition dipoles, and excitation-induced forces, while TDDFT predicts more extended excitons; differences diminish under compression.
watch_item: Agreement depends on nuclear configuration, with marked QMC–BSE discrepancies where predicted exciton localization differs substantially.
paper_title: Excitons in solid molecular hydrogen from quantum Monte Carlo
